findings.summary: The red route keeps a private copy of the Reader proxy request-header allowlist and forwarding loop.
findings.consequence: Reader asset proxy header policy now has to be changed in both server/routes/red/[...path].ts and server/utils/reader-source-proxy.ts; a future update to conditional, range, or hop-by-hop filtering can silently diverge between /red and the sibling /txt, /bilder, and /export/faksimil routes.
findings.evidence: contentRequestHeaders at lines 48-57 defines the same allowlisted request headers and Connection-token exclusion pattern as readerRequestHeaders in server/utils/reader-source-proxy.ts lines 190-199. The sibling routes server/routes/txt/[...path].ts, server/routes/bilder/[...path].ts, and server/routes/export/faksimil/[...path].ts all delegate through proxyReaderSourceRequest, so /red is the only asset route maintaining this policy locally.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared request-header allowlist/forwarding helper from reader-source-proxy and use it from the red route, or route /red through a shared Reader proxy helper while keeping only the intentional /red path-canonicalization behavior separate if that behavior must remain.
